Developmental exposure of rats to physiologically patterned magnetic fields (7 Hz, square wave, 1-50nT) resulted in increased brain weight and body weight in young adults.

the long-term biological effects of developmental exposure of the fetus to physiologically- patterned magnetic fields (7 Hz square wave) and the possible role of nitric oxide in mediating these effects.

there is a lack of conclusive evidence for any biological effects of MFs.
the effects of MFs on the development of the rat are not well understood and require further investigation.
developmental exposure to a 7 Hz, square wave MF has long-term effects on brain, body and testis weights.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of MFs are not intensity-windowed, but that the effects of NO modulation are.
developmental exposure to physiologi- cally-patterned magnetic fields can affect the structure and function of the brain and reproductive system.
the long-term effects on the brain, body and testes are more pronounced in 5-50 nT groups, and that the effects of NO modulation are more pronounced in the 5-10 nT groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of MFs on the developing organism are not simply a function of intensity.
the effects of developmental MF exposure on behaviour are not short-term, and that these effects may not be reversible in adulthood.
developmental exposure to physiologic MFs may have subtle long-term effects, and that these effects may depend on NO activity in the developing organism.
